title: Maximizing business value with AI-driven data strategies
summary: Learn how an AI-driven data strategy turns scattered data into a decision engine, plus practical steps to align data, AI, and business goals.
body_markdown:
#### Short on time? Read the key takeaways:


- Data is the most important ingredient of agentic AI, with a well-structured data strategy supporting data-driven decision-making.
- Thoroughly understanding data and its ecosystem helps optimize your use of internal, synthetic, and external datasets.
- Aligning AI strategy with your organization’s overall business strategy and objectives makes it easier to identify business opportunities and revenue streams.
- Start small with an AI project that is manageable and achievable. Then, experiment, iterate, and continuously assess AI model performance to improve your approach.


#### Data strategy has been part of the business conversation for years. Agentic AI just raised the stakes. It rewards good data fast, and it punishes bad data even faster.


Ninety percent of organizations now say they have the right architecture to support large-scale, data-driven decision-making, up from 72% just a year earlier, according to[Unisys's 2026 AI & Cloud Insights Report](https://www.unisys.com/report/unisys-ai-cloud-insights-report-2026/) . Yet only 65% report operational efficiency exceeding expectations, down from 80% in 2025.


That gap is where strategy matters most. Closing it starts with treating data as a strategic asset, the same way factories, equipment, and real estate already are. Fed a diet of diverse, high-quality data,[AI models](https://www.unisys.com/solutions/artificial-intelligence/) learn to spot patterns and relationships that turn directly into new insights and business outcomes, recognizing data's inherent value and freeing it from the silos where it's trapped.


“Building a strong technology foundation is an important first step. IT and business leaders must show that their investments are paying off and delivering real growth,” **said Unisys Chief Executive Officer and President Mike Thomson in the report.**


### What is an AI-driven data strategy?


An AI-driven data strategy is an organization's plan for collecting, governing, and activating data so AI systems can turn it into actionable business insights. It covers where data lives, how it's governed, who can access it, and how AI models and agents consume it to support decisions across the business. The strategies below show how to put one into practice.


### Adopt a data-driven culture and mindset


A data-driven culture supports better decision-making and continuous improvement. Such a culture is only fully realized when[data analytics](https://www.unisys.com/solutions/cai/data-analytics/) are common across roles in your organization and not exclusive to the data team. Storytelling can smooth the transition between the science of data and the art of business when championing best practices and sharing news of business wins.


### Treat data as an asset


High-quality data contributes to more successful AI implementation. Treating data as an asset means knowing where to source it, how to store it, and how to strengthen its accuracy and integrity. It also means assigning clear owners who are accountable for each critical dataset. Doing so helps organizations uncover new opportunities, improve efficiency, and drive innovation.


A[leading health and security services firm](https://www.unisys.com/our-clients/m/deploying-a-next-generation-data-ingestion-platform-on-aws/) , with more than 1,000 locations in 80+ countries, wanted to turn scattered data into a true decision engine. The firm worked with Unisys to consolidate its data into a cloud-native enterprise data lake capable of feeding analytics and visualization tools, third-party integrations, and web and mobile applications. The resulting data ingestion platform delivered:


- 98% improvement in the quality of ingested data
- HIPAA-compliant architecture
- 100% adherence to data privacy and security requirements
- Successful onboarding of 4,500 enterprise customers via 45 million ingested employee data points


### Gain insights from all your data


All too often, data is scattered across the enterprise, trapped in siloed systems and inaccessible to AI models. To get full value from internal, synthetic, and external datasets, especially for using with agentic AI, you need a clear picture of what data you have, where it lives, and how reliable it is. Synthetic data, which algorithms generate instead of collecting it through real-world observation, can fill gaps when real data is scarce, sensitive, or regulated.


AI is changing how organizations turn all that data into real, actionable insights, including through tools like[AI-powered document processing](https://www.unisys.com/video/cis/take-the-difficulty-out-of-document-processing/) and curated knowledge management systems. These tools matter because much of an organization's most useful knowledge sits in unstructured content, such as documents, emails, and transcripts.


Your data ecosystem should include a flexible data architecture, which lets you access data wherever it is and across various formats, including real-time streaming and unstructured..


### Prepare your data for agentic AI


Instead of answering a single question, agentic AI plans and carries out multistep tasks, pulling data from several systems along the way, which makes it useful to some of the most demanding data consumers in the enterprise.


Interest is high, but adoption is still early. In the[Unisys AI & Cloud Insights Report 2026](https://www.unisys.com/report/unisys-ai-cloud-insights-report-2026/) , 75% of organizations say agentic AI will be essential to managing cloud environments, yet only 23% have begun scaling it across the business. Data management and integration issues (26%) rank among the top barriers.


To get your data ready for agentic AI:


- **Add context:** Maximizing quality while minimizing assumptions and hallucinations, agentic AI needs to know what data means as well as where it sits. A shared semantic layer and well-maintained metadata help agentic AI interpret data consistently.
- **Deliver data in real time:** Agents that act on stale data make stale decisions[. Gartner predicts](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-06-16-gartner-identifies-the-top-trends-for-data-and-analytics) adoption of data streaming for agentic AI will climb beyond 60% by 2028, from under 15% in 2025.
- **Govern access and decisions:** Define what data agentic AI can reach and which decisions it can make on its own, and keep a record of what it did and why.


### Make data accessible, actionable, and outcomes-driven


Prioritizing data-driven decision-making and treating agentic AI as a strategic asset drives faster, more informed decisions while fostering innovation. It works best when business and technology teams share ownership of the outcomes.


Providing self-service access to a common data layer for reliable, consistent, and high-quality information lets employees across the organization use data actively in decision-making. The same data layer can serve AI models and agents, giving them governed access to the data each use case requires.


Conversational AI interfaces put these insights in the hands of frontline workers and other team members, so your organization can respond faster when market conditions or customer needs change.


### Align business and AI strategy


Align AI strategy with your overall business strategy to ensure that AI initiatives support the organization’s objectives and deliver measurable results. A well-designed AI strategy helps an organization identify new business opportunities and revenue streams.


Take these steps as part of your strategy:


- Consider the ethical, organizational, leadership, cultural, and legal implications of AI strategy implementation.
- Create a roadmap for developing, deploying, and scaling AI applications, and define the business metrics you’ll use to measure success.
- Set up[change management for a successful implementation](https://www.unisys.com/solution-brief/dws/organizational-change-management/) .
- Prioritize use cases by business value and data readiness. Some will call for predictive analytics, others for generative AI or AI agents.


Generative AI is now mainstream, which gives employees without technical training a conversational way to ask questions of data. Agentic AI is the next step, with systems that take action across workflows within limits you set. Both raise the bar for data quality, context, and governance


Cloud AI platforms let organizations fine-tune models for their industry or ground them in enterprise data through retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), then deploy them across internal apps for content generation, summarization, semantic search, and code generation.


### How to advance your AI strategy


Use these three practices to turn your data into a driver of business outcomes:


**1. Start small, experiment, and iterate**


Begin with an AI project that is manageable and achievable and iterate as you go, testing your AI models and refining them based on the results. Build feedback loops so models and agents can be retrained or adjusted as new data arrives and business goals shift.


**2. Plan for implementation and ongoing monitoring**


Evaluate your AI systems and continuously assess the performance of your AI models against the business metrics you set at the start, such as cost, cycle time, or customer satisfaction, and improve them as needed.


**3. Prioritize transparency**


Build transparency into your AI applications so people can understand and explain the decisions that models and agents make. Taking a responsible and ethical approach to AI means following[responsible AI principles](https://www.unisys.com/blog-post/ai/how-to-implement-responsible-ai-responsibly/) and checking that your AI applications comply with legal standards, such as privacy and data security regulations. As agents take on more decisions, treat security and governance as enablers.

## FAQs


It's an organization's plan for collecting, governing, and activating internal, synthetic, and external data so AI systems can turn it into actionable business insights, aligned with overall business objectives.


AI models learn by finding patterns in the data they're fed. High-quality, diverse data helps models identify accurate patterns and relationships; siloed or poor-quality data limits the insights AI can generate, regardless of volume.


Start small with a manageable, achievable project, then experiment and iterate. Continuously assess model performance and refine your approach based on results rather than trying to scale everything at once.


Agent-ready data is accurate, governed, and rich in context, so AI agents can interpret it correctly, access it when they need it, and act on it within defined permissions.
